sources.root_cause_summary: Unsigned subtraction wrap in NTLM type-3 size guard bypasses stack buffer overflow prevention

summary: Buffer capacity guard using unsigned subtraction of a runtime value from a compile-time constant wraps on large values, making the guard always pass and allowing a subsequent memcpy to overflow a fixed-size stack buffer.

unsafe: Guard using unsigned subtraction `size < (capacity - len)` wraps when the runtime length exceeds capacity, bypassing bounds checking and allowing unbounded memory copies
Memory copy of a runtime-controlled length into a fixed-size stack buffer at a runtime offset without adequate bounds validation
safe: Guard using additive comparison `len + offset > capacity` avoids unsigned wrap by computing total size first
Pre-validation of the runtime length against buffer capacity before any comparison with remaining capacity
Signed arithmetic in size guards where a negative subtraction result correctly fails the check

anchors.behavior: Comparison guarding a memory copy where the right-hand side subtracts a runtime value from a buffer capacity constant using unsigned arithmetic
anchors.inspect_hint: Verify that the subtracted runtime value can exceed the buffer capacity constant, causing unsigned wrap of the result and making the comparison always pass. Check the types of all operands—size_t and unsigned int will wrap; signed types would produce a negative value that correctly fails the guard.

anchors.behavior: Memory copy of a runtime-determined number of bytes into a fixed-size stack buffer at a runtime offset
anchors.inspect_hint: Check whether the guard condition preceding this copy can be bypassed via unsigned integer wrap. Evaluate whether the copy length plus offset exceeds the buffer capacity. Verify that the guard uses additive or signed arithmetic rather than unsigned subtraction.
